title: Anthony Colandrea, Nebraska offense sharpen up in dominant win over Bowling Green
content:
LINCOLN, Neb. — Nebraska beat Bowling Green 56-7 Saturday night at Memorial Stadium, a first-half dismantling of a low-level MAC team after a few season-opening hiccups a week earlier.

The Huskers are 2-0 with FCS opponent North Dakota on tap in Lincoln next week ahead of the conference opener at Michigan State.

The outcome itself Saturday — amid patriotic pregame and postgame theatrics to honor America’s 250th birthday — means next to nothing in the Huskers’ bid this fall to elevate their program in the Big Ten hierarchy.

Nebraska outgained Bowling Green 369 yards to 46 in the first 30 minutes.

But certain elements of the win do matter.

“That’s the way we thought we should play,” coach Matt Rhule said.

Let’s have a look inside:

Nebraska came out with a crisp and clean approach, Rhule said, that was missing in its 49-21 season-opening win against Ohio. Despite a turnover on the second play when a pass intended for Jacory Barney was intercepted, there was no doubt early about the Huskers’ bad intentions.

First-year quarterback Anthony Colandrea threw darts. He completed difficult passes for four touchdowns as Nebraska built a 35-0 lead. He finished 20-for-24 for 222 yards, hitting Barney and Kwazi Gilmer for two scores apiece.

Colandrea was decisive with his throws. The UNLV transfer showed touch on the touchdown passes to Barney, connections of 35 and 32 yards in opposite corners of Tom Osborne Field. And Colandrea displayed precision on the throws to Gilmer. The UCLA transfer, with three touchdown catches in two games, caught scoring passes of 12 and 4 yards in the end zone.

On the first, Colandrea sliced a pass between Bowling Green defenders.

And on the second Gilmer TD, which put Nebraska up 21-0 midway through the second quarter, Colandrea fired a strike as the receiver dove toward the east sideline of the north end zone. It was a high-difficulty play featuring a quick release from the QB.

“I thought that throw was absolutely outrageous,” Rhule said.

It was a perfectly executed, high-difficulty play featuring a quick release from the QB.

“Try to put it out there and let him make a play,” Colandrea said.

That, exactly, is what Nebraska coaches wanted to see against the mismatched Falcons: execution that will translate against a treacherous Big Ten slate.

Speaking of that Big Ten schedule, perhaps it turned a touch more manageable Saturday. Few in college football expect the Huskers to go into Eugene, Ore., and win in five weeks. But the Ducks’ loss at Oklahoma State at least provides hope.

And Illinois’ home loss to Duke raises questions about the Illini, who play host to Nebraska on Nov. 6. And another Nebraska road foe, Rutgers, continues to nose-dive early this season.

To be clear, there’s nothing easy about playing three teams that made the College Football Playoff a year ago and finishing the season at Iowa. But if the early returns are an indication, the Big Ten will deliver surprises in the weeks ahead.

Iowa and Washington earned close victories. Top-ranked Ohio State blew a three-score lead to lose 24-23 at No. 4 Texas. All are Nebraska opponents this year.

The Huskers will gladly take a seven-touchdown margin — regardless of the opponent.

“Has anybody watched the Big Ten right now?” Rhule said. “We’re not winning a ton of games.”

First-year coordinator Rob Aurich said after the opener that the Huskers needed to play faster. They did. With anchor Owen Chambliss back from a hamstring injury to make his Nebraska debut, the Blackshirts flew to the football against Bowling Green.

Gone was the hesitancy. Chalk it up to Week 1 jitters. If this was the Aurich-era style, it’s going to be a fun ride. The Huskers held Bowling Green to 46 yards in the first half.

The Falcons chose early to challenge cornerback Andrew Marshall, the Huskers’ best defender last week, according to Aurich. That failed. And from there, Eddie George’s squad appeared to have little direction offensively against a swarming unit.

Chambliss, the San Diego State transfer who came with Aurich, and Oregon State transfer Dexter Foster were especially active at linebacker. Foster knived through the line for a tackle for loss in the second quarter. Marshall cut down a receiver for a 1-yard gain on third-and-2.

“We talk about bleeding the cut out,” defensive back Donovan Jones said “You want to keep going at that eye.”

Jones intercepted Jay Kastantin on Bowling Green’s second offensive possession, coming down with a ball tipped by Williams Nwaneri at the line of scrimmage. And reserve linebacker Derek Wacker converted a 25-yard scoop-and-score TD in the fourth quarter.

The running game for Nebraska showed well again. After Mekhi Nelson, Isaiah Mozee and Jamal Rule totaled 329 yards and five scores on 35 touches in the opener, the three-back system flourished against Bowling Green to the tune of 239 yards and two touchdowns on 27 touches.

“It’s not the Big Ten yet,” Rhule said.

All inexperienced before this season, they’re playing like vets.

Rule followed up his big debut by busting a 59-yard touchdown run en route to 88 yards on eight carries. Nebraska held him out of the second half. Nelson continued to display his versatility with back-to-back catches on screen passes during a first-half touchdown drive. He totaled 82 yards on 10 touches. And Mozee chipped in with effective play, scoring his first career touchdown on a 7-yard run in the fourth quarter.

Nebraska produced a second consecutive 35-point half in the first two quarters, then lacked the same sharpness after halftime. But the tone was set early.

Not everything went well. The Huskers were sluggish on special teams, committing holding penalties — against Mario Buford, Braylen Prude and Wacker — on three consecutive punt returns.

Rhule took the blame for the flags on special teams. He said he must direct the Huskers’ adjustments to tighter officiating on returns.

Nebraska was flagged seven times for 65 yards after it was called for nine penalties in the opener. A holding call against Barney wiped out a 45-yard keeper for a touchdown by Colandrea on Nebraska’s opening snap of the third quarter. And center Justin Evans was flagged for holding on the same possession, which ended with Kyle Cunanan missing a 55-yard field-goal attempt.
